subject: Scoped Log Disposition & CAIQ Mapping Request — Clearmind Health
messages:
From: Laura Meyers <security@clearmindhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@clearmindhealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify log retention evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is doing a final pass on CAIQ and SIG artifacts and needs a concise exhibit that explains how Redwood handles session and inference-stub logs for Clearmind's tenant (multi-tenant hosted). Specifically:

- Exact retention windows for: request/response payload traces, inference intermediate caches (KV cache metadata), and ephemeral debug traces.
- The deletion workflow and proof-of-delete for tenant-scoped logs (we tend to require a programmatic erasure token or manifest).
- Any customer-specific exception process (legal hold / forensic preservation) — who owns approvals and what timeline to expect.

Could you provide an evidentiary packet (PDF + mapping spreadsheet) and an attestation draft we can include with our CAIQ submission? Procurement will also need the scope called out for contract redlines.

Appreciate a timeline — our deadline for the submission is EOD Friday.

Best,
Laura Meyers
Security Program Manager
Clearmind Health

Attachment: examples of CAIQ rows they expect (reference only)
From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Laura Meyers <security@clearmindhealth.com>, Jake Liu <jake.liu@clearmindhealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log retention evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (product / compliance lead) and Markus (legal ops) who will own the artifacts and the attestation draft.

Quick answers while they pull the packet:
- Standard hosted default: request/response traces retained 30 days; ephemeral debug traces 7 days; KV-cache metadata stored transiently (session-window only) and not persisted beyond 24 hours by default.
- We can provide a signed proof-of-delete manifest generated from our deletion job that contains per-tenant deletion timestamps and checksums.
- For legal hold / forensic preservation we have an exception workflow: customer raises a request via the Console (Support -> Preservation), Security approves (SLA 48 hrs), and Ops triggers a preservation snapshot — preservation is governed by a written approval retained in the ticket.

Marissa/Markus — can you confirm we can produce: (1) CAIQ mapping spreadsheet filtered to Clearmind scope, (2) a one-page deletion attestation (Redwood letterhead), and (3) an exportable proof-of-delete manifest sample plus the retention policy excerpt. Laura — is PDF + one XLSX enough?

Sergio
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, Laura Meyers <security@clearmindhealth.com>, Jake Liu <jake.liu@clearmindhealth.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log retention evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi all — attaching the first draft pack for Clearmind. Included:

1) clearmind_sig_mapping_v1.xlsx — CAIQ/SIG rows we mapped to Redwood controls.
2) session-log-retention-exhibit.pdf — concise exhibit (policy text + retention matrix + sample manifest).
3) redwood-deletion-attestation-draft.docx — editable attestation for legal review.

Notes / deviations called out in the spreadsheet:
- We default to 30/7/1 (request traces / ephemeral debug / KV metadata) but can configure tenant-level TTL up to 365 days for request traces under Dedicated or Private plans (requires written justification).
- The proof-of-delete manifest contains: tenant_id, object_path, deletion_timestamp (ISO8601), deletion_job_id, SHA256 of exported artifact. We redact minimal PII from the manifest for privacy, but full manifests can be delivered under NDA.
- For preservation requests we log an approval artifact in the ticketing system; the approval is required before preservation snapshots are taken. Typical turnaround we’ve observed: 24–72 hours depending on scope.

Action items for Clearmind: please confirm whether you need (A) full manifest delivery under NDA, (B) only a sample manifest in the attestation, or (C) acceptance of redacted manifest plus ticket evidence. We can start the formal attestation once legal confirms wording in the DOCX.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this helps. Quick clarifications from procurement/legal side:

- We prefer option (A) under NDA, but need to limit frequency to a one-time delivery plus quarterly snapshots. Can you confirm Redwood can automate a quarterly manifest delivery to a secure S3 bucket?
- For the attestation, Clearmind requires the attestation to reference our tenant_id and include a signature block for Redwood's legal counsel.

Procurement also flagged a contract redline around the definition of "ephemeral debug traces" — they want it explicitly excluded from backups and archives.

If you can confirm automation and the attestation wording, we'll route the DOCX to our legal for review.

Jake Liu
Senior Legal Counsel
Clearmind Health
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: Jake Liu <jake.liu@clearmindhealth.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify log retention evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Jake — we can commit to the following in writing (subject to standard contract and NDA provisions):

1) One-time full manifest delivery to a Clearmind-controlled secure S3 location; thereafter quarterly automated manifest snapshots (CSV, gzipped) per tenant_id. We will include a manifest schema and delivery keys.
2) Attestation: we will produce the attestation on Redwood letterhead with tenant_id inserted and include a signature line for Redwood General Counsel. Draft attached to the packet (redwood-deletion-attestation-draft.docx).
3) "Ephemeral debug traces" will be explicitly defined and excluded from backups/archives in the attestation and the redline. The definition will match the product doc: traces created during active debugging sessions that are not persisted beyond 7 days and are not part of long-term telemetry.

I'll have Legal drop a redline of the DOCX by EOD tomorrow. Marissa — please prepare the automation runbook (S3 delivery + encryption details) so we can include it with the CAIQ submission.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
